reference.title: Band standing crunch
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read; the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching: facing a high band anchor, hands by the forehead)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you curl down, breathe in as you stand back up.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, short squeeze, 1.4 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 2-3 reps short of failure (clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen: step back from the anchor for more tension
prescription.progression: Stronger band, longer squeeze, slower return

cues.text: Face the anchor, band looped high over the bar. Feet hip width, knees soft. Hold the band in both hands by the forehead, elbows forward and down.
Breathe out and curl the ribs down toward the pelvis, rounding the upper back; the hands stay by the forehead.
Squeeze the abs at the bottom; hips stay over the feet, knees soft.
Breathe in and uncurl slowly back to tall standing, controlling the band.
Stand tall for a moment, then curl again.

mistakes.mistake: Hinging at the hips instead of curling the spine
mistakes.fix: Think ribs to pelvis; the hips barely move.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling the band down with the arms
mistakes.fix: Keep the hands fixed by the forehead; the trunk does the work.
Keep the chin slightly tucked and the head in line with the upper back.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap you upright

kinematics.norm: Curl through the spine (mostly thoracic and upper lumbar), as in the floor curl-up (Escamilla 2016; clinical opinion for the standing version)
Small: the hips stay over the feet (clinical opinion)
Fixed by the forehead, elbows forward (clinical opinion)
Controlled, with a slower return (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Band standing crunch, video (movement reference)
Escamilla et al. 2016, muscle activation among supine, prone and side position exercises with and without a Swiss ball (Sports Health 8(4):372-379)
Oliva-Lozano and Muyor 2020, core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Check the band and the anchor before each set: the band runs close to the face, and a band that slips or snaps can hit you.
Repeated loaded spinal flexion is a concern for people with disc problems (McGill 1998): keep the range moderate or choose an anti-extension exercise instead.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low back discomfort: smaller curl, more knee bend.
Neck discomfort: keep the hands at the forehead and do not pull the head down.
progressions: Kneeling band crunch for more range.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis curls the ribs toward the pelvis against the band; transversus abdominis braces. Curl-up type exercises put most of their load on the rectus abdominis (Escamilla 2016; Oliva-Lozano 2020 review).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Help the trunk curl and keep it square (clinical opinion; obliques work with the rectus in curl-ups, Escamilla 2016).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Help the trunk curl and keep it square (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Small hip bend as the trunk curls (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Small hip bend as the trunk curls (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Hold the arms steady against the band (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Hold the arms steady against the band (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Hold the elbows against the band's pull (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Hold the elbows against the band's pull (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Keep the hips under the trunk (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Keep the hips under the trunk (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Lengthen as the spine rounds and control the return (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Lengthen as the spine rounds and control the return (clinical opinion).
